label_note: Hand-authored synthetic relevance grades defined before the recorded model answers. These are not independently reviewed real-world judgments. Identity and C-lifetime cases have manual adjudications; other cases also have deterministic grading checks in the original experiment.

development/identity-effective-access.criterion: Prioritize these independent identity configurations for review of effective access. Evaluate the named subject at 2026-01-15T12:00:00Z, using only the listed rules. A rule applies only to its exact resource and action unless it explicitly says all; applicable explicit denies override allows. Assume no unlisted grants, memberships, trust, or rules. Highest priority: the subject can currently perform identity.write on resource Cedar (environment production), directly or through an explicitly permitted role-assumption chain. Next: it can identity.write on resource Birch (environment staging), but not Cedar. Next: it can identity.read on Cedar, but neither of those writes. Lowest: none of those abilities. Expired sessions and unsatisfied conditions cannot grant access.

development/code-lifetime-priority.criterion: Prioritize the C snippets for memory-lifetime review. Treat each snippet independently. All allocations succeed. consume(int x) only uses its integer argument; choose() returns either 0 or 1; release(int *p) is exactly free(p); touch(int *p) is exactly *p = 7. Prioritize in this order: an unconditional write through a pointer to freed storage; then an unconditional read from freed storage with no such write; then a read or write from freed storage possible only for some choose() outcomes; then snippets with no read or write from freed storage. A double-free alone is outside this particular criterion. Use C pointer aliasing and control flow, not variable names. Ignore allocation leaks and uninitialized values.

development/telemetry-chain-evidence.criterion: Rank the independent telemetry bundles by strength of this specified chain. The target chain is an accepted interactive login for account morgan on endpoint Larch, followed within 120 seconds by a process on that same endpoint and session_id, followed within 30 seconds of that process by a network connection on the same endpoint and process_guid to destination 203.0.113.42:443. Timestamps are UTC, with interval endpoints inclusive. A process event is eligible only when parent_image=sshd; its image and command text are otherwise irrelevant. Highest: all three linked stages exist. Next: the accepted login and eligible process link exists, but no qualifying connection. Next: at least one accepted target login exists, but no eligible linked process. Lowest: no accepted target login exists. Do not join by numeric pid alone or borrow facts between bundles. Events may appear out of chronological order.

engine/build-impact-heldout.criterion: Prioritize independent build-change records by the strongest impacted output. An edge "A uses B" means a change to B can affect A, transitively. A change propagates toward users, never toward its dependencies. The changed node is listed explicitly; consider only listed edges and output labels, and assume every listed dependency is active. Highest: some output labeled production is impacted. Next: no production output is impacted, but an output labeled staging is. Next: no production or staging output is impacted, but an output labeled development is. Lowest: none of the labeled outputs is impacted. Cycles are allowed. A changed output impacts itself. Node names do not imply environment labels.

engine/service-window-policy-heldout.criterion: Prioritize these independent service snapshots under the following exact operational policy. Evaluate only environment=production, region=east, and the currently serving revision in deployment.serving_revision. A matching observation must cover exactly [2026-03-12T12:00:00Z,2026-03-12T12:05:00Z]. Do not combine observations. A confirmed breach is a matching observation with at least 100 requests and an error rate strictly greater than 2 percent. A provisional breach is a matching observation with 1 to 99 requests and an error rate strictly greater than 2 percent. A rollback is eligible only if rollback.from_revision equals the serving revision, rollback.ready is true, rollback.target_health is passing, and rollback.valid_until is later than 2026-03-12T12:05:00Z. Highest priority: confirmed breach with eligible rollback. Next: confirmed breach without eligible rollback. Next: provisional breach and no confirmed breach. Lowest: neither breach. Ignore metric rows and rollback information that do not meet the listed conditions.

engine/dependency-advisory-heldout.criterion: Prioritize these independent dependency snapshots for a specific advisory affecting package identity (registry=npm, name=cedar-core), stable versions at least 2.4.0 and strictly below 2.7.3. Compare each numeric SemVer component as an integer; all versions here are stable releases. A package is reachable from an application only by following enabled dependency edges in the listed direction. A runtime path contains only edges with kind=runtime. A build path contains at least one edge with kind=build. Use installed package identity, not a local alias or node ID. Highest: an affected package is reachable by a runtime path from an application with environment=production. Next: an affected package is reachable by a runtime path from staging, but not production. Next: an affected package is reachable by any enabled path from an application, but neither prior condition applies. Lowest: no affected package is reachable from any application. Disabled edges cannot be used. Unlisted dependencies and applications do not exist.
